name: Recursive Arbitration and Conflict Resolution Law
purpose: Define local arbitration behavior among competing continuation possibilities.

candidate_law_statement.informal: Recursive arbitration resolves conflicts among competing continuation possibilities by applying local admissibility, budget, reinforcement, perturbation, and invariant-preservation constraints.

formal.candidate_set: Q_α := { q_i : q_i is an admissible continuation candidate at or reachable from α }
formal.arbitration_operator_candidate: Arb_A(Q_α) := selected, deferred, split, merged, pruned, or collapsed continuation subset under local admissibility constraints
formal.conflict_condition: Conflict(Q_α) occurs when simultaneous persistence of candidates exceeds admissibility budget, violates boundary compatibility, or destabilizes preserved invariants.
formal.priority_score_candidate: Priority_A(q_i) := F(admissibility_margin, reinforcement_support, finite_flux_cost, perturbation_resilience, invariant_preservation, reconstruction_accessibility)
formal.tie_resolution_condition: Tie(Q_α) may preserve multi-branch continuation, defer selection, invoke local tie-break rules, or maintain ambiguity when priority scores remain equivalent within tolerance.
formal.nonunique_clause: Arbitration is not assumed unique, deterministic, globally optimal, or final.
formal.recursive_clause: Arbitration outcomes feed back into future admissibility budgets, reinforcement channels, and topology transitions.
